member.name: T:HumanGateway.Core.Cursor.CursorMath
member.summary: Pure cursor arithmetic shared by the sync engine. Cursor advancement is safe: a receiver only advances its position over sequences it has actually applied, so a gap in the stream never causes a loss (SYNC-FR-06, SYNC-FR-07). This is the deterministic reordering/convergence primitive behind out-of-order tolerance.

member.name: M:HumanGateway.Core.Cursor.CursorMath.AdvanceContiguous(HumanGateway.Core.Cursor.CursorPosition,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.Int64})
member.summary: Advances contiguously over the sequences present in . Starting from prior.Sequence + 1, the cursor advances one step at a time while the next sequence is present; it stops at the first gap. This means out-of-order batches converge without loss: a batch carrying {1, 3} advances the cursor to 1, and the later batch carrying {2} advances it to 3.
member.remarks: Sequences at or below prior.Sequence are ignored (already covered). Callers must supply the receiver's own prior position (decoded from the echoed sinceCursor), not the batch's span.

member.name: T:HumanGateway.Core.Idempotency.IdempotencyKeys
member.summary: Deterministic idempotency-key derivation (SYNC-FR-02). The key identifies a logical batch by durable identity — the batch ID plus each item's kind, sequence, and durable ID — not by payload bytes. A retry that re-sends the same items therefore derives the same key (so the receiver collapses it as a replay), while a change to the batch ID or to an item's durable identity yields a new logical batch. Payload integrity (tamper/change detection) is the content hash's job, verified separately (also SYNC-FR-02). The result is a sha256:<hex> hash, matching the schema's ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$ shape.

A replayed batch derives the same key; changing the batch ID or an item's durable identity (e.g. a message ID) yields a new key. Mutating an item's payload leaves the key unchanged.

member.name: T:HumanGateway.Core.Idempotency.IIdempotencyStore
member.summary: Deduplication port for replayed sync batches (SYNC-FR-02, NF-05). A retry of the same batch MUST reuse the same batchId AND idempotencyKey; changing either creates a new logical batch (syncbatch.schema.json). The store makes applying a batch idempotent so at-least-once delivery yields exactly-once effect.
member.remarks: Implementations must be atomic under concurrency (e.g. a unique index on (batchId, idempotencyKey) in SQLite/PostgreSQL). The in-memory reference implementation in this assembly locks for single-process use.
